author: naomitzhao
body:
# 97 - [PR View][Timeline] Collapse commits

Closes #97 

## Description

This pull request automatically truncates long commit messages and adds a button that toggles showing the expanded version of the commit message.

### Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/461702fa-c550-4eec-a640-a16ac8602e05

## Changes

### `useOverflows.ts`

Creates a hook that checks whether an element's contents overflows, used to check if a commit message's contents overflow its container.

### `TimelineDisplay.tsx`

Create new component `ExpandableCommitText` to implement the expandable commit feature. 

### `TimelineDisplay.module.css`

Rename `.committedLine` to `.timelineCommit` for readability. Create new style classes `.expandableCommitText`, `.commitMessage`, and `expandButton` to implement the expandable commit text.

### `TimelineDisplay.module.css`, PR View `page.module.css`

Add `min-width: 0;` to override lack of `flex-shrink`. Otherwise, the commit messages in the timeline will not be bound and will grow infinitely in width with `flex`.

## Next steps

Since the width of commit messages is based on overflow calculation before mounting, the commit message component size will not be responsive with window size changes. This may require event listeners on each commit message or a rework to use a fixed length character limit for commit messages (like how GitHub implements it, 69-character limit). :(

author: kajanth
body:
## 💡 What
Replaced interactive `<div>` and `<span>` elements used as triggers (like `#dream-state`, `.api-ep-item`, and API history rows) with native `<button type="button">` elements in `web/dashboard.html`. Added CSS resets (`border: none`, `background: transparent`, `appearance: none`, etc.) to maintain the original design.

## 🎯 Why
Using non-interactive elements like `div` or `span` for buttons creates accessibility barriers. It forces screen readers to guess intent or rely on manually bolted-on `role="button"` attributes, and it breaks native keyboard accessibility (like activating with the Spacebar or Enter key) unless custom `onkeydown` listeners are added. Using native `<button>` elements provides this functionality automatically.

## 📸 Before/After
Visually, the UI remains exactly the same due to the CSS resets. However, functionally, users can now reliably tab to and activate these elements with their keyboards.

## ♿ Accessibility
- **Native Keyboard Support:** Elements can now be triggered natively via Space and Enter keys without custom JavaScript event handlers.
- **Screen Reader Semantics:** Screen readers will naturally announce these elements as interactive buttons.
- **Focus Management:** Focus rings and tab-order are inherited natively from the browser engine.

author: akutuva21
body:
# Modernize parallel computing APIs and improve MCMC swap strategy

## Summary

This PR modernizes PTempEst's parallel computing infrastructure for compatibility with current MATLAB releases (R2014a+) and improves MCMC mixing by replacing the deterministic chain swap sweep with a randomized even-odd pairing scheme.

## Motivation

- `matlabpool` was deprecated in R2013b and removed in R2014a, making `parallel_tempering.m` unable to run in parallel on any modern MATLAB version.
- The original deterministic high-to-low swap sweep can introduce systematic correlations between successive swap decisions within a single round, potentially slowing convergence.
- Chain initialization and per-experiment energy evaluations were serial even when a parallel pool was available.

## Changes

### Parallel computing modernization
- **`parallel_tempering.m`**: Replaced `matlabpool('local', nlabs)` with `parpool('local', nlabs)`, guarded by `gcp('nocreate')` to reuse an existing pool. Replaced `matlabpool close` with `delete(gcp('nocreate'))`.
- **`init_chains.m`**: Converted the chain initialization loop to `parfor` with local temporary variables (`tmp_energy`, `tmp_params`) for correct `parfor` variable classification. Worker count respects `cfg.parallel` and `cfg.maxlabs`.
- **`energy_gaussian.m` / `energy_tdistr.m`**: Converted the experiment simulation loop to `parfor`. Replaced illegal `return` statements (not permitted inside `parfor`) with per-experiment energy accumulation via `expt_energy` array and `continue`. Per-experiment `tic`/`toc` timers replace the old single `simtimer` so the time penalty uses sum-of-simulation-times rather than wall-clock time. Removed the resulting dead `simtimer` variable. Worker count respects `cfg.parallel` and `cfg.maxlabs`.

### Swap strategy improvement
- **`parallel_tempering.m`**: Replaced the deterministic descending sweep (`cfg.nchains : -1 : 2`) with a randomized even-odd scheme that randomly selects whether to pair chains `(1,2), (3,4), ...` or `(2,3), (4,5), ...` each round. This is a standard technique in replica exchange methods to reduce inter-swap correlations.
- **`parallel_tempering.m`**: Swap attempts are now tracked with a tri-state encoding in `swap_acceptance`: `0` = not attempted, `-1` = attempted and rejected, `1` = attempted and accepted.
- **`adapt_beta.m` / `display_chains.m`**: Updated swap acceptance rate calculations to use `acceptances / max(attempts, 1)` instead of `acceptances / cfg.adapt_beta_interval`, so the adaptive temperature ladder correctly targets the configured `optimal_swap_acceptance` rate relative to actual attempts.

## Behavioral notes

- **Serial mode is unaffected.** When `cfg.parallel = 0`, all `parfor` loops execute as ordinary `for` loops (MATLAB's `parfor(i=1:N, 0)` semantics).
- **Pool reuse.** The new code reuses an existing parallel pool if one is open, even if its worker count differs from `nlabs`. The original code always opened a fresh pool.
- **Time penalty semantics.** The energy time penalty now uses the sum of per-experiment wall times rather than total wall-clock time for the loop. In parallel mode this will be larger than wall time (sum of overlapping durations), preserving roughly the same penalty magnitude as serial execution.
- **Swap attempts per round.** The even-odd scheme attempts ~`nchains/2` swaps per round (half the original `nchains-1`). Each pair is still attempted with equal frequency on average across rounds. The `adapt_beta` calculation has been updated to account for this.
- **`fprintf` in `parfor`.** Chain initialization output may appear interleaved when running in parallel. This is cosmetic only.

## Testing

- Verified that all modified files parse without errors in MATLAB R2023b.
- Confirmed serial mode (`cfg.parallel = 0`) produces identical behavior to the unpatched code.
- Confirmed parallel mode launches a pool, distributes work across workers, and completes without errors.
- Validated that `adapt_beta` receives correct acceptance rates under the new tracking scheme by inspecting `swap_acceptance` and `beta_history` outputs.

author: copilot
body:
`groszeWidth` values for 18 money fields (pages 2 and 4) were 40–57 px too large, placing the gr input boundary well to the left of the form's printed comma. Right-column fields were visually broken: the gr input spanned most of the cell while the zł input was cramped and clicks near the comma landed on gr instead of zł.

## Root cause
Previous commit computed `groszeWidth` incorrectly. The correct value is `field.x + field.w − comma_x` — the distance from the *printed comma* to the wrapper's right edge. Old values (102–110 px) were nearly double the actual gr column width (~46–61 px).

## Fix
Pixel-scanned each form page image to locate the printed comma character per field, then applied `groszeWidth = wrapper_right − comma_x`:

| Fields | Page | Old | New | zł% / gr% |
|--------|------|-----|-----|-----------|
| 67–76 | 2 | 102 | 56 | 73 / 27 |
| 193, 195 | 4 | 103 | 57 | 73 / 27 |
| 194, 196 | 4 | 103 | 61 | 71 / 29 |
| 199, 201 | 4 | 71, 48 | 46 | 78 / 22 |
| 204 | 4 | 110 | 52 | 76 / 24 |
| 205 | 4 | 66 | 46 | 78 / 22 |

Schema-only change (`pit36.json`). No code modifications.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds a complete CI/CD pipeline for the research-to-production AI workflow with human-in-the-loop capabilities.

### Changes:

1. **GitHub Actions Workflow** (.github/workflows/research-to-production-pipeline.yml)
   - Automated weekly research gap analysis
   - Deep research prompt generation for AI agents
   - Human review ticket creation via GitHub issues
   - Research alignment configuration updates

2. **Configuration Files**
   - config/research-alignment.json: Research priorities and coverage thresholds
   - config/core-concepts.json: Core framework concepts definition

3. **Python Scripts**
   - scripts/analyze_research_coverage.py: Research gap analyzer
   - scripts/generate_deep_research_prompt.py: Deep research prompt generator
   - scripts/update_research_alignment.py: Research alignment updater
   - scripts/generate_research_pipeline_report.py: Pipeline report generator

4. **Documentation**
   - docs/research-pipeline/README.md: Complete pipeline documentation

### Human-in-the-Loop Workflow:

1. **Automated Analysis**: Pipeline runs weekly or on-demand
2. **Gap Detection**: Identifies missing or insufficient research coverage
3. **Prompt Generation**: Creates specific, actionable research prompts
4. **Human Review**: GitHub issue created for human evaluation
5. **Decision Point**: Human decides which prompts to pass to AI agent
6. **AI Research**: Approved prompts sent to deep research AI agent
7. **Integration**: Research findings incorporated into framework

### Key Features:

- Automated gap detection against core framework concepts
- Configurable research focus (quantum_core, ternary_computing, moe_routing, etc.)
- Multiple depth levels (quick, standard, comprehensive, exhaustive)
- Explicit exclusion of AI ethics concerns
- Human approval required before AI agent research
- Continuous refinement through weekly cycles
- Full audit trail via GitHub issues and artifacts

### Research Focus Areas:

1. **Quantum Core**: Qutrit stabilizer formalism and GF(3) operations
2. **Ternary Computing**: 1.58-bit ternary state space and arithmetic
3. **MoE Routing**: Tropical geometry Mixture-of-Experts routing
4. **Flash-CIM**: Flash compute-in-memory integration
5. **SYCL Acceleration**: Multi-core GPU/CPU acceleration
6. **Forward-Forward Learning**: Teacherless self-supervised learning
7. **Cognitive Ergonomics**: WUI design principles for complex systems

### Testing:

The pipeline can be tested by:
1. Manually triggering the workflow via GitHub Actions
2. Running the scripts locally with test data
3. Reviewing the generated reports and prompts

### Related Issues:

This pipeline addresses the need for continuous research alignment and automated gap detection in the q_mini_wasm_v2 framework.

### 💡 What
- Associated form labels with inputs using the `for` attribute.
- Upgraded the progress area to be a polite live region with dynamic `aria-valuenow` updates.
- Empowered the custom drag-and-drop zone with full keyboard and mouse accessibility, avoiding interaction bugs.
- Recorded a critical finding about dropzone event handling in the Palette journal.

### 🎯 Why
- Screen readers rely on semantic `<label for="id">` associations to properly announce form inputs.
- Without `aria-live`, dynamic progress updates remain invisible to assistive technologies.
- Custom drop zones (built from standard `<div>` elements) fail keyboard navigation and interaction without explicit roles, tab indexes, and event listeners. The implementation specifically prevents a known issue where clicking an inner button causes a bubbling double-trigger on the hidden file input.

### ♿ Accessibility
- Full WCAG compliance on form controls, live regions, and custom interactive widgets.

author: michaeljancsy
body:
## Summary
- Fix two WaveNet buffer bugs (ping-pong addressing, cross-array head accumulation order)
- Move NAM inference from WASM sandbox to native host via `__conjuredsp_nam_process` import
- Add native Accelerate support to `conjuredsp` accel module
- Simplify `nam!()` macro: removes 4MB WASM buffer, uses host import instead
- Optimize conjuredsp in debug builds (`opt-level = 3`) — unoptimized NAM was 15x slower
- Invalidate WasmCache when rlib changes
- Zero-copy host import: NamModel reads/writes WASM memory directly as f32 slices

## Root causes
1. **Buffer bugs**: ping-pong addressing (2nd+ layer array read wrong region), cross-array head accumulation (broadcast-add before rechannel, not after)
2. **WASM sandbox overhead**: NAM inference inside WASM had correctness issues with host imports
3. **Debug optimization**: conjuredsp crate compiled without optimizations in Debug builds — 77ms vs ~5ms for 471 stereo frames (15x penalty)

## Test plan
- [x] 259 Rust tests pass (156 conjure_dsp + 103 conjuredsp-rs)
- [x] 278 Swift tests pass
- [x] Python-vs-Rust parity: 0.000000 error for tiny and standard WaveNet models
- [x] WASM→host e2e integration test: 0.000000 error
- [x] Manual: Rust NAM preset plays audio within budget, comparable to Python

author: copilot
body:
Subspace was missing fundamental engine infrastructure (input, audio backend, threading, asset management, AI composition, scene management) that NovaForge (MasterRepo) had fully implemented. This PR ports those systems, adapted from C++20 to C++17, wired into the existing `subspace::` namespace and ECS.

## New systems

### Core infrastructure
- **`core/math`** — `Vector2`, `Matrix4`, `Quaternion` (slerp, euler, axis-angle, lookAt, perspective/ortho projection)
- **`core/memory`** — `LinearAllocator` (O(1) bump-pointer + `Reset()`) and `PoolAllocator<T,N>` (O(1) free-list, compile-time capacity)
- **`core/events/EventBus`** — type-safe `type_index`-keyed pub/sub; parallel to existing string `EventSystem` to avoid breaking ~15k lines of game code
- **`core/serialization/BinaryArchive`** — read/write binary archive for trivially-copyable types and `std::string`; SFINAE-based (C++17, no concepts)
- **`core/threading/TaskSystem`** — fixed-size thread pool, `Submit(fn) → std::future<void>`, inline fallback when uninitialised
- **`core/assets/AssetManager`** — ref-counted typed asset registry; `Load<T>`, `Get<T>`, `Unload`, `GarbageCollect`
- **`core/world/Level`** — named loadable scene wrapping `EntityManager`; `OnLoad`/`OnUnload` callbacks; enables main-menu, sector transitions, and save/load scoping

### Input
- **`input/`** — `Keyboard`, `Mouse`, `Gamepad` (per-frame pressed/released/down), `InputSystem` (named action bindings), `InputComponent` (ECS snapshot for gameplay systems)

### Audio backend
- **`audio/SoundAsset` + `SoundBank`** — typed sound registry by id and name
- **`audio/AudioDevice`** — device init with Null backend (OpenAL hook point ready)
- **`audio/AudioMixer`** — 64-channel logical mixer; volume/pan/loop/priority; auto-expire non-looping channels on `Update(dt)`
- **`audio/SpatialAudio`** — 3D positional audio; clamped inverse-distance attenuation; stereo pan from listener orientation

### AI
- **`ai/BehaviorTree`** — `BTSequence` (AND), `BTSelector` (OR), `BTParallel` (N-of-M), `BTInverter`, `BTLeaf` (callback), `BTCondition` (predicate); `BehaviorTree` driver; composable alternative to monolithic `AIDecisionSystem`

### UI
- **`ui/widgets/`** — `Widget` (parent/child hierarchy, layout, visibility), `WidgetTree` (root driver), `ButtonWidget` (click callback), `TextInputWidget` (editable, max-length, onChange), `TreeViewWidget` (expandable nodes)

### Physics
- **`physics/CharacterController`** — capsule AABB, gravity integration, ground detection, step-height; `Move()` returns collision-resolved position; `Teleport()`; `CharacterControllerComponent` with serialization

## Build
- `CMakeLists.txt` updated: all new `src/` subdirs added to `GLOB_RECURSE`, `Threads::Threads` linked for `TaskSystem`
- 222 new tests added to `test_main.cpp`; total 3944 tests, 0 failures

## Usage example

```cpp
// Behavior tree composing patrol + combat logic
auto root = std::make_shared<BTSelector>();

auto patrol = std::make_shared<BTSequence>();
patrol->AddChild(std::make_shared<BTCondition>([&]{ return !threatNearby; }));
patrol->AddChild(std::make_shared<BTLeaf>([&](float dt){ return DoPatrol(dt); }));

auto combat = std::make_shared<BTLeaf>([&](float dt){ return DoCombat(dt); });

root->AddChild(patrol);
root->AddChild(combat);

BehaviorTree bt;
bt.SetRoot(root);
bt.Tick(deltaTime); // replaces monolithic score table in AIDecisionSystem
```

author: smoreinis
body:
## Summary - **Add background FIFO queue** for async span processing — `AsyncTrace.start_span()` and `end_span()` no longer await processor HTTP calls inline, removing 8 blocking round-trips per request - **Wire graceful shutdown** into FastAPI lifespan so the queue drains before server exit ## Problem Users reported high latency with tracing enabled. Datadog showed significant time spent in `/v5/spans/batch` — every span start/end awaited HTTP calls to tracing processors inline. With 4 spans per request and 2 events each, that's 8 blocking network round-trips per request just for telemetry. ## Solution New `AsyncSpanQueue` class in `span_queue.py` with: - Synchronous `enqueue()` via `put_nowait` — callers return instantly - Background drain task processing events sequentially (FIFO ordering preserves SGP processor's start-before-end invariant for its internal `_spans` dict) - Error logging via `asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` — processor failures don't crash the drain loop - Graceful `shutdown(timeout)` using `Queue.join()`, wired into FastAPI lifespan teardown in `base_acp_server.py` ## Test plan - [x] 7 tests for span queue (non-blocking enqueue, FIFO ordering, error resilience, shutdown drain, timeout, post-shutdown safety, AsyncTrace integration) - [x] Full test suite passes (598 passed, 959 skipped) - [x] Lint + typecheck clean

Greptile Summary

This PR removes 8 blocking HTTP round-trips per request by introducing `AsyncSpanQueue` — a background FIFO drain task that processes span start/end events asynchronously while preserving the start-before-end ordering required by the SGP processor. Graceful drain-before-exit is wired into the FastAPI lifespan via `shutdown_default_span_queue`. The previous concern about a shared mutable `Span` reference racing with the background drain task has been resolved: both `start_span` and `end_span` now enqueue a `span.model_copy(deep=True)`, fully decoupling the live span object from the background processor. Key observations: - The FIFO invariant and error isolation (`return_exceptions=True` + per-result logging) are correctly implemented. - Graceful shutdown via `Queue.join()` + cancel is a sound pattern; the `_ensure_drain_running` restart guard adds resilience if the drain task ever unexpectedly terminates. - The queue is **unbounded** (`asyncio.Queue()` with no `maxsize`), which could lead to uncapped memory growth under sustained processor latency. - The shutdown warning logs `qsize()`, which excludes the one item currently being processed by the drain task — the count can be off by one. - The `30.0`-second default timeout is duplicated across `AsyncSpanQueue.shutdown` and `shutdown_default_span_queue`; extracting it to a named constant would avoid drift. - Test coverage is solid: 7 tests covering non-blocking enqueueing, FIFO ordering, error resilience, drain-on-shutdown, timeout, post-shutdown drops, and end-to-end `AsyncTrace` integration.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge; all remaining findings are non-blocking P2 style/hardening suggestions. No P0 or P1 issues found. The core race condition from the previous review round is addressed by deep-copying spans before enqueue. Shutdown sequencing, FIFO ordering, and error isolation are all correctly implemented. The three P2 comments (unbounded queue, off-by-one warning count, duplicated magic number) are improvements worth making but do not affect correctness or production safety of the feature. src/agentex/lib/core/tracing/span_queue.py — review the unbounded queue and shutdown warning accuracy.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/agentex/lib/core/tracing/span_queue.py | New AsyncSpanQueue class; well-structured FIFO drain loop with error isolation and graceful shutdown, but the queue is unbounded, the shutdown warning miscounts in-flight items, and the 30.0s timeout magic number is repeated. | | src/agentex/lib/core/tracing/trace.py | Async processor calls replaced with span_queue.enqueue(); span is deep-copied before enqueuing (addressing previous mutable-reference concern), and the optional span_queue parameter threads through cleanly. | | src/agentex/lib/core/tracing/tracer.py | Minimal change: span_queue parameter added to AsyncTracer.trace() and passed through to AsyncTrace; no issues. | | src/agentex/lib/sdk/fastacp/base/base_acp_server.py | Lifespan wrapped in try/finally to call shutdown_default_span_queue on teardown; graceful drain wired correctly. | | tests/lib/core/tracing/test_span_queue.py | 7 tests covering non-blocking enqueue, FIFO ordering, error resilience, shutdown drain, timeout, post-shutdown safety, and AsyncTrace integration; good coverage of core invariants. | | src/agentex/lib/core/tracing/__init__.py | Exports updated to include AsyncSpanQueue, get_default_span_queue, and shutdown_default_span_queue; no issues. |

Sequence Diagram

author: kizabgd123
body:
### 💡 What:
The optimization replaces O(N) log file reading in `JudgeGuard` with O(1) tail retrieval. Instead of reading the entire `WORK_LOG.md` file into memory just to extract the last 1000 or 15000 characters, the code now seeks directly to the end of the file and reads backwards.

### 🎯 Why:
As the project grows, the `WORK_LOG.md` file continuously expands. Reading the entire file for every `JudgeGuard` verification (which happens for every critical action) causes linear performance degradation and increases memory usage.

### 📊 Impact:
- **Reduces latency by ~1700x** for large log files (10MB+).
- Constant memory overhead regardless of log size.
- Prevents $O(N)$ CPU/IO spikes during agent-turn verification.

### 🔬 Measurement:
- Verified via `tests/benchmark_log_retrieval.py`.
- 10 iterations on a 10MB log:
  - Before: ~0.8s
  - After: ~0.0005s
- Existing tests (`tests/test_judge_guard.py`) passed.

author: abelonogov-ld
body:
## Summary

Extends session replay to capture non-spatial press interactions (tvOS Siri Remote, D-pad, hardware keyboard, keyboard-window touches) and encode them as RRWeb custom events alongside existing touch replay.

### What changed

**Capture layer (`LaunchDarklyObservability`)**

- `PressInteraction` — replaces `PressSample`; adds `.keyboard` kind for hardware keyboard presses; `isKeyboard` computed property covers `.keyboard` and `.untrackedWindowTouch`
- `InteractionEvent` — unified `.touch` / `.press` enum replacing the old touch-only `PassthroughSubject`
- `UserInteractionManager` — single `interactionEvents` publisher replaces the old `publisher` + separate subject
- `InputCaptureCoordinator` — press events emitted on `.began` only (no redundant `.ended`); `.other` kind filtered out but `.keyboard` passes through
- `PressInterpreter` — converts `UIPress`/`UITouch` system-uptime timestamps to Unix epoch (same approach as `TouchInterpreter`)

**Transport layer (`LaunchDarklySessionReplay`)**

- `PressInteractionPayload` — `EventQueueItemPayload` with `SessionReplayExporter`; routes through the same `EventQueue` as touches
- `SessionReplayService` — subscribes to `interactionEvents`, dispatching touches and presses into the queue

### RRWeb wire contract

| Tag | When | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| `RemoteControl` | Siri Remote, D-pad, game controller press | `{ "pressType": "select" }` (+ optional `pressTypeSystemRaw`) |
| `Keyboard` | Hardware keyboard key or keyboard-window touch | `{}` (empty — tag carries the semantics) |

Both are `EventType.Custom` (type 5). Backend stores them as opaque JSON. Web player ignores unknown tags unless extended.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds a new interaction type and RRWeb custom event encoding for keyboard/remote presses, changing the session replay event stream and wire payloads. Risk is moderate due to potential compatibility issues with downstream ingestion/player expectations and timestamp conversion logic.
> 
> **Overview**
> Session replay now captures *non-spatial press interactions* (remote controls, hardware keyboard presses, and touches on untracked windows like keyboard chrome) and exports them alongside existing touch replay.
> 
> On the capture side, `PressSample` is replaced by `PressInteraction` (including a new `.keyboard` kind) and a new `PressInterpreter` normalizes press timestamps to Unix time; press/touch forwarding is unified via an ordered `InteractionEvent` stream from `UserInteractionManager`.
> 
> On the export side, presses are queued via `PressInteractionPayload` and encoded by `RRWebEventGenerator` as a new RRWeb custom tag `Press` with a `PressPayload` that records the press `source` (remote vs physical/software keyboard) plus optional remote `pressType`/raw type; decoding support and tests were added for this new custom event.
>

author: xdustinface
body:
When the SPV client broadcasts a transaction, connected peers never relay it back because Dash Core marks the sender as already having the transaction. This meant broadcast transactions were invisible in the client's mempool state until a restart triggered a full mempool re-fetch.

Add `dispatch_local()` to `NetworkManager` to inject messages into the local message pipeline. `broadcast_transaction()` now checks sync state, broadcasts to peers, then injects the tx locally so `MempoolManager::handle_tx()` processes it through the existing path.

The sentinel peer address (`0.0.0.0:0`) signals a self-originated transaction, causing `handle_tx` to call `record_send` automatically. A dedup guard skips transactions already tracked in `mempool_state`.

Also adds `SyncError::NotSynced` for rejecting broadcasts before sync completes, and a `create_signed_transaction` test helper for building transactions without broadcasting via `dashd`.

author: copilot
body:
Adds a fully automated data pipeline that replaces the manually-curated `data/animals.geojson` with real OSM POI data enriched from Wikipedia/Wikidata, output in the same GeoJSON schema the frontend already consumes.

## Pipeline architecture

**Medallion layers (DuckDB + dbt):**
- **Bronze** — raw Overpass elements loaded as-is into `raw_osm_elements`
- **Silver** — filters by animal-identifying tags (`zoo`, `animal`, `species`, `wikidata`, `wikipedia`), excludes the outer zoo boundary, extracts structured columns from JSON tags
- **Gold** — JOINs silver with `wiki_enrichment`, slugifies IDs, builds Wikipedia URLs, shapes to output schema

**Python scripts:**
- `download_osm.py` — builds Overpass QL from `$BBOX`/`$OSM_TAGS`, caches response by query hash, loads into DuckDB
- `enrich_wiki.py` — fetches Wikidata P225 (taxon), P18 (image), Wikipedia summary per POI; caches each entity individually
- `export_geojson.py` — queries `gold_animals`, validates, writes `data/animals.geojson`

## Configuration via environment variables

| Variable | Default |
|---|---|
| `BBOX` | `52.490,13.495,52.525,13.545` (Tierpark Berlin) |
| `OSM_TAGS` | `zoo,tourism=zoo,animal,species` |
| `OVERPASS_URL` | `https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter` |
| `OUTPUT_PATH` | `data/animals.geojson` |
| `WIKIDATA_LANG` | `en` |

## GitHub Actions (`pipeline.yml`)

Triggers on `workflow_dispatch` (with input overrides), weekly schedule, and push to `pipeline/**`. Caching strategy:
- **OSM cache key**: SHA-256 of `BBOX|OSM_TAGS` — survives until query parameters change
- **Wiki cache key**: ISO week number — refreshes weekly to pick up edits

Auto-commits updated `data/animals.geojson` back to `main` with `[skip ci]` to avoid deploy loop.

author: nick-skriabin
body:
Xyron Shell Integration

Adds native integration with Xyron shell when `[xyron] enabled = true` in config. Xyron runs as the PTY shell with a sideband IPC socket for smart features like autocompletion.

How it works

- When enabled, Attyx spawns Xyron as the shell instead of the default (zsh/bash)
- Xyron auto-enables IPC when it detects ATTYX=1 in the environment
- Xyron emits OSC 7339 events through the PTY for socket discovery and CWD changes
- Attyx connects to Xyron's IPC socket, performs a handshake, and receives push events
- Completion candidates are rendered as a cursor-anchored overlay using the declarative UI system

Config

```
[xyron]
enabled = true
# path = "/custom/path/to/xyron"   # optional, auto-detects from PATH
```

Detection order: xyron.path config → ~/Projects/xyron/zig-out/bin/xyron (dev builds) → PATH lookup.

Features

- Shell integration: Xyron runs in both session and non-session modes. New tabs spawn Xyron. Session daemon receives Xyron as the shell program.
- OSC 7339 parsing: New parser support for xyron: events — ipc_ready (socket path), cwd_changed (working directory for statusbar widgets).
- IPC handshake: Bidirectional socket exchange — Attyx sends its ctl-*.sock path + pane ID, Xyron confirms with name/version.
- Completion overlay: Xyron pushes evt_overlay_show/update/dismiss (0xB0-0xB2) through Attyx's IPC server. Rendered as a cursor-anchored dropdown with the declarative Menu component. Dynamic width based on candidate text, selection highlight with readable contrast.
- IPC client: Full query API for completions, ghost text, history, shell state, and jobs — ready for future features.

Architecture

```
  Attyx                           Xyron (PTY shell)
    │                                │
    ├─ spawns xyron in PTY ──────────┤
    │                                ├─ detects ATTYX=1, enables IPC
    │                                ├─ emits OSC 7339 ipc_ready
    ├─ parses socket path ◄──────────┤
    ├─ sends handshake (0x12) ──────►├─ stores attyx socket path
    │                                │
    │  [user presses Tab]            │
    │                                ├─ gathers completions
    │                                ├─ sends evt_overlay_show (0xB0)
    ├─ receives via ctl-*.sock ◄─────┤    to attyx's IPC server
    ├─ renders overlay               │
    │                                ├─ sends evt_overlay_dismiss (0xB2)
    ├─ hides overlay ◄───────────────┤
```

body:
## Summary

Complete implementation of the Canary Fleet per `docs/arch/rivers-canary-fleet-spec.md`. A 6-app Rivers bundle that exercises every API surface point and fails loudly when something breaks.

### Profiles (6 apps, 80 test endpoints)

| Profile | App | Port | Tests | What it validates |
|---------|-----|------|-------|-------------------|
| AUTH | canary-guard | 9100 | 9 | Guard view, session lifecycle, CSRF, token size |
| SQL | canary-sql | 9101 | 19 | PG/MySQL/SQLite CRUD, param binding order, DDL rejection, caching |
| NOSQL | canary-nosql | 9102 | 13 | MongoDB, ES, CouchDB, Cassandra, LDAP, Redis CRUD + admin rejection |
| RUNTIME | canary-handlers | 9103 | 26 | ctx.* surface, Rivers.* globals, V8 security, StorageEngine |
| STREAM | canary-streams | 9104 | 9 | WebSocket, SSE, Streaming REST, Kafka, Polling |
| PROXY | canary-main | 8080 | 4 | Cross-app HTTP proxy, session propagation, error format |

### Key test traps
- Parameter binding order: all SQL DataViews use `$zname` before `$age` to catch alphabetical sort bugs (Issue #54)
- DDL rejection: `DROP TABLE` via `execute()` blocked by Gate 1
- V8 timeout: handler runs `while(true){}` to test watchdog termination
- V8 code gen: verifies `Function()` constructor is blocked
- Error sanitization: verifies no IP/port leaks in error responses
- Admin op rejection: Redis `FLUSHDB` and MongoDB `drop_collection` blocked

### SPA Dashboard
canary-main includes a Svelte SPA at `/` that fetches all test endpoints and displays a pass/fail grid.

microsoft/playwright (@​playwright/test) ### [`v1.59.1`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.59.1) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/compare/v1.59.0...v1.59.1) ##### Bug Fixes - **\[Windows]** Reverted hiding console window when spawning browser processes, which caused regressions including broken `codegen`, `--ui` and `show` commands ([#​39990](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/39990)) ### [`v1.59.0`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.59.0) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/compare/v1.58.2...v1.59.0) #### 🎬 Screencast New [page.screencast](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-screencast) API provides a unified interface for capturing page content with: - Screencast recordings - Action annotations - Visual overlays - Real-time frame capture - Agentic video receipts
**Screencast recording** — record video with precise start/stop control, as an alternative to the [`recordVideo`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context-option-record-video) option: ```js await page.screencast.start({ path: 'video.webm' }); // ... perform actions ... await page.screencast.stop(); ``` **Action annotations** — enable built-in visual annotations that highlight interacted elements and display action titles during recording: ```js await page.screencast.showActions({ position: 'top-right' }); ``` [screencast.showActions()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-show-actions) accepts `position` (`'top-left'`, `'top'`, `'top-right'`, `'bottom-left'`, `'bottom'`, `'bottom-right'`), `duration` (ms per annotation), and `fontSize` (px). Returns a disposable to stop showing actions. Action annotations can also be enabled in test fixtures via the `video` option: ```js // playwright.config.ts export default defineConfig({ use: { video: { mode: 'on', show: { actions: { position: 'top-left' }, test: { position: 'top-right' }, }, }, }, }); ``` **Visual overlays** — add chapter titles and custom HTML overlays on top of the page for richer narration: ```js await page.screencast.showChapter('Adding TODOs', { description: 'Type and press enter for each TODO', duration: 1000, }); await page.screencast.showOverlay('
Recording
'); ``` **Real-time frame capture** — stream JPEG-encoded frames for custom processing like thumbnails, live previews, AI vision, and more: ```js await page.screencast.start({ onFrame: ({ data }) => sendToVisionModel(data), size: { width: 800, height: 600 }, }); ``` **Agentic video receipts** — coding agents can produce video evidence of their work. After completing a task, an agent can record a walkthrough video with rich annotations for human review: ```js await page.screencast.start({ path: 'receipt.webm' }); await page.screencast.showActions({ position: 'top-right' }); await page.screencast.showChapter('Verifying checkout flow', { description: 'Added coupon code support per ticket #​1234', }); // Agent performs the verification steps... await page.locator('#coupon').fill('SAVE20'); await page.locator('#apply-coupon').click(); await expect(page.locator('.discount')).toContainText('20%'); await page.screencast.showChapter('Done', { description: 'Coupon applied, discount reflected in total', }); await page.screencast.stop(); ``` The resulting video serves as a receipt: chapter titles provide context, action annotations highlight each interaction, and the visual walkthrough is faster to review than text logs. #### 🔗 Interoperability New [browser.bind()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browser#browser-bind) API makes a launched browser available for `playwright-cli`, `@playwright/mcp`, and other clients to connect to. **Bind a browser** — start a browser and bind it so others can connect: ```js const { endpoint } = await browser.bind('my-session', { workspaceDir: '/my/project', }); ``` **Connect from playwright-cli** — connect to the running browser from your favorite coding agent. ```bash playwright-cli attach my-session playwright-cli -s my-session snapshot ``` **Connect from [@​playwright/mcp](https://redirect.github.com/playwright/mcp)** — or point your MCP server to the running browser. ```bash @​playwright/mcp --endpoint=my-session ``` **Connect from a Playwright client** — use API to connect to the browser. Multiple clients at a time are supported! ```js const browser = await chromium.connect(endpoint); ``` Pass `host` and `port` options to bind over WebSocket instead of a named pipe: ```js const { endpoint } = await browser.bind('my-session', { host: 'localhost', port: 0, }); // endpoint is a ws:// URL ``` Call [browser.unbind()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browser#browser-unbind) to stop accepting new connections. #### 📊 Observability Run `playwright-cli show` to open the Dashboard that lists all the bound browsers, their statuses, and allows interacting with them: - See what your agent is doing on the background browsers - Click into the sessions for manual interventions - Open DevTools to inspect pages from the background browsers.
- `playwright-cli` binds all of its browsers automatically, so you can see what your agents are doing. - Pass `PLAYWRIGHT_DASHBOARD=1` env variable to see all `@playwright/test` browsers in the dashboard. #### 🐛 CLI debugger for agents Coding agents can now run `npx playwright test --debug=cli` to attach and debug tests over `playwright-cli` — perfect for automatically fixing tests in agentic workflows: ```bash $ npx playwright test --debug=cli ### Debugging Instructions - Run "playwright-cli attach tw-87b59e" to attach to this test $ playwright-cli attach tw-87b59e ### Session `tw-87b59e` created, attached to `tw-87b59e`. Run commands with: playwright-cli --session=tw-87b59e ### Paused - Navigate to "/" at output/tests/example.spec.ts:4 $ playwright-cli --session tw-87b59e step-over ### Page - Page URL: https://playwright.dev/ - Page Title: Fast and reliable end-to-end testing for modern web apps | Playwright ### Paused - Expect "toHaveTitle" at output/tests/example.spec.ts:7 ``` #### 📋 CLI trace analysis for agents Coding agents can run `npx playwright trace` to explore [Playwright Trace](https://playwright.dev/docs/trace-viewer) and understand failing or flaky tests from the command line: ```bash $ npx playwright trace open test-results/example-has-title-chromium/trace.zip Title: example.spec.ts:3 › has title $ npx playwright trace actions --grep="expect" # Time Action Duration ──── ───────── ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ──────── 9. 0:00.859 Expect "toHaveTitle" 5.1s ✗ $ npx p

author: rentchaincanada
body:
This update introduces the TransUnion redirect handshake contract and callback integrity layer on top of the existing provider-agnostic screening architecture, without enabling any live TransUnion integration or altering the current tenant-facing UX.

The focus of this phase is to formalize redirect lifecycle management, secure callback handling, and replay-safe session resolution, ensuring the system is ready for activation once TransUnion confirms integration details.

🔐 Redirect Handshake Foundation
Defines a complete redirect lifecycle model for screening sessions:
session creation → redirect preparation → provider return → callback resolution
Introduces structured handling for:
stateToken
correlationId
redirectUrl
returnUrl
expiresAt
Adds a provider-neutral redirect preparation layer, ensuring:
sessions are validated before redirect
redirect metadata is consistently generated and stored
future providers can reuse the same handshake model
🧠 State Token & Correlation Model
Implements secure state token generation and lookup
cryptographically strong tokens
server-side resolution only
expiration-aware
Standardizes correlation across:
screening request
screening session
provider session (future)
callback resolution
Ensures safe mapping between redirect initiation and callback completion
🔁 Callback Integrity & Replay Protection
Adds hardened callback handling with:
duplicate callback detection and safe ignore behavior
replay protection via token/session validation
expired token rejection
mismatch detection (token ↔ session ↔ request)
Prevents mutation of:
completed sessions
unrelated sessions
invalid or stale flows
Adds audit events for:
redirect_prepared
callback_received
callback_duplicate_ignored
callback_rejected
return_state_resolved
📊 Normalized Return & Result Contract
Defines a provider-agnostic return state model:
completed
pending
action_needed
expired
unable_to_complete
Extends result normalization contract to support future TU mapping:
normalizedDecision
identityVerified
creditIncluded
incomeIncluded
fraudFlags
summary
reportAvailability
Ensures frontend continues to consume normalized data only, with no provider coupling
🧩 TU Adapter Enhancement (Still Disabled)
Expands TransUnionRedirectAdapter scaffold to align with handshake contract:
structured session creation
callback handling hooks
normalization contract
All TU functionality remains:
disabled via config
non-networked
non-impacting to runtime behavior
⚙️ Routing & Safety
Confirms provider routing remains:
centralized
config-driven
fail-safe (manual fallback remains default)
Ensures redirect flow cannot activate unless explicitly enabled
🎯 Frontend Stability
No user-facing UX changes introduced
Tenant dashboard and messaging flows remain unchanged
Minimal type support added for future redirect/return states
✅ Result

This PR completes Phase 1.2 (Handshake & Activation Prep) by:

establishing a secure, replay-safe redirect handshake model
preparing the system for TransUnion redirect activation
maintaining full provider-agnostic flexibility
preserving stable tenant UX and safe fallback behavior

author: ivanangelsegurafernandez
body:
### Motivation
- Fix a bug where, when a protection pause expired, the same update loop could immediately retrigger a new 30m pause because signals (drawdown/EMA/structure) were still in the adverse state.
- Implement a minimal, local latch to block rearming for the same stale event while preserving all existing protection semantics and published JSON fields.

### Description
- Added four globals next to the existing protection globals: `PROTECTION_REARM_COOLDOWN_S = 90.0`, `PROTECTION_REARM_DD_RELEASE_MARGIN_PCT = 0.50`, `protection_rearm_blocked = False`, and `protection_last_release_ts = 0.0`.
- Introduced a new function `_equity_protection_recovery_ok(structure_trigger: bool = False) -> bool` that returns True only if there is a real recovery by drawdown margin or EMA (and returns False while `structure_trigger` is True), and is robust to missing/None values.
- Modified `_equity_protection_is_active(...)` to, upon pause expiration, set `protection_rearm_blocked = True`, set `protection_last_release_ts = now_ts`, and log: `PROTECCION_SALDO: FINALIZADA | maestro reanudado | rearme bloqueado hasta recuperación`.
- Modified `_equity_protection_update(...)` to follow the requested flow: compute `active_now`, compute `raw_trigger`, if `protection_rearm_blocked` evaluate `recovery_ok` and `cooldown_ok` and only clear the latch when both are satisfied (logging `PROTECCION_SALDO: REARME HABILITADO | recuperación confirmada`), and only then allow the existing activation path to run unchanged.
- No other logic/architecture/JSON fields were changed; `protection_health_state.json` fields `active`, `reason`, `started_ts`, `until_ts`, `time_left_s`, `drawdown_pct`, and `resume_text` remain intact and compatible with `monitor_saldo_pro.py`.

### Testing
- Compiled both files with `python -m py_compile 5R6M-1-2-4-8-16.py monitor_saldo_pro.py` and the compilation succeeded without errors.
- Searched for and verified presence of the new globals, new function, and expected log strings with `rg` and those searches returned the inserted symbols and messages as expected.
- Verified via `rg` that the protection state payload keys (`"active"`, `"reason"`, `"started_ts"`, `"until_ts"`, `"time_left_s"`, `"drawdown_pct"`, `"resume_text"`) are still present in the code paths that write the JSON.
- No automated behavioral tests were added; the change is a minimal surgical patch limited to `5R6M-1-2-4-8-16.py` and preserves compatibility with `monitor_saldo_pro.py`.

## Summary

Nightly automated code simplification sweep of the \`TranscriptedMCP\` tool (MCP server added in the last 3 commits on this branch).

- **Extracted \`frontmatterBlock()\` helper** — YAML frontmatter boundary detection was copy-pasted in both \`extractTitle\` and \`handleReadMeeting\`'s speakers case. Now shared.
- **Extracted \`extractDialogueLines()\` helper** — the \`## Full Transcript\` section parsing was duplicated in \`handleReadMeeting\` and \`handleRecap\`. Now unified.

author: veksen
body:
## Summary

The CI comment's "X queries analyzed" disagreed with the query list on the site — most dramatically on the [sin-bot PR 12 run](https://github.com/veksen/sin-bot/pull/12), which reported **4236 queries analyzed** in the PR comment while the site showed **74**.

Root cause: the reported count was computed at ingest time from the number of `plan:` log entries that passed filtering, not from the number of unique queries we actually analyze. The same 74 distinct queries ran ~57× each across 457 vitest specs, inflating the headline by ~57×.

This change:

- Computes `queryStats.analyzed` (renamed from `queryStats.total`) using `buildQueries(allResults, config).length` — the exact same list used to upload to the site, so the headline always matches what the user sees.
- Drops the separate `total` counter from the ingest loop.
- Drops the `countUploadableQueries` / `UPLOADABLE_STATES` helpers — they duplicated the filter that already lives in `buildQueries`.
- Restores the `Matched N unique queries out of M log entries` debug log by using `recentQueries.length` (no extra counter needed).
- Updates `ReportStatistics.total` → `ReportStatistics.analyzed` (docstring: "Number of unique queries analyzed and uploaded to the site"). Consumers updated in the success template and test fixtures.

## Why this is the right fix

Before deciding on the dedup approach, we added a diagnostic step to sin-bot's CI workflow that split the log by phase and counted `plan:` / `pg_catalog` / `information_schema` / `@qd_introspection` lines. Results on the sin-bot run:

| Phase                   | `plan:` entries | pg_catalog hits | info_schema hits | @qd_introspection |
| ----------------------- | --------------: | --------------: | ---------------: | ----------------: |
| `drizzle-kit migrate`   |              41 |              38 |                0 |                 0 |
| `npm test` (457 specs)  |            4220 |              95 |                0 |                 0 |

Key takeaways that shaped this PR:

1. **Migration phase is tiny.** 41 plan entries. The initial theory that drizzle-kit introspection was inflating the count does not hold.
2. **No `information_schema` traffic reaches `plan:` entries** in either phase.
3. **The 4220 test-phase entries are real application queries**, executed by the test suite. 457 specs × ~9 queries each ≈ 4100.
4. **The headline mismatch is purely about dedup**, not filtering. A pre-count `isSystemQuery` / `information_schema` filter would not have materially moved the number.

Given that, delegating to `buildQueries` is strictly better than any heuristic filter: there is one filter definition (in `site-api.ts`), and the CI comment is guaranteed to report whatever we actually uploaded.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/runner.test.ts src/reporters/github/github.test.ts` passes (20/20)
- [x] Existing template rendering tests updated for the `total` → `analyzed` rename
- [x] New `runner.test.ts` asserts `buildQueries(allResults).length` counts exactly the queries reported to the site on a mixed-state input
- [x] Re-run sin-bot PR 12 against this branch and confirm the PR comment reports 74 (or whatever the current analyzed count is) rather than a 4-digit number

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

- Consider surfacing the ingest-count elsewhere (e.g. in the Query Doctor run page) if users find the "executions vs. uniques" ratio useful for understanding test-suite shape.
- The diagnostic write-up lives at `.context/query-count-handoff.md` in this workspace and documents the ruled-out hypotheses so we don't retrace them.

body:
## Summary

Rewrites `process.stdin`/`process.stdout`/`process.stderr` initialization to closely match Node.js's `lib/internal/bootstrap/switches/is_main_thread.js`:

- **Lazy getter properties**: `process.stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin` are now lazy getters (matching Node.js's `defineStream` pattern), breaking the circular dependency between `process` and `node:net`/`node:fs`
- **Handle-type-based stream creation**: `createWritableStdioStream(fd)` switches on `guessHandleType(fd)`:
  - `TTY` -> `tty.WriteStream(fd)`
  - `PIPE`/`TCP` -> `net.Socket({ fd, writable: true })`
  - `FILE` -> sync fd write stream via `op_node_fs_write_sync`
- **stdin same pattern**: `createStdin()` switches on type: `TTY` -> `tty.ReadStream`, `PIPE`/`TCP` -> `net.Socket({ fd })`, `FILE` -> `fs.ReadStream`
- **Removes `deno_io` usage** from `_process/streams.mjs` entirely
- **Removes TTY-specific branching** from `process.ts` boot path

Closes https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/33131

author: copilot
body:
Community groups with verified Meetup/Luma source claims had no recurring sync — admins had to manually trigger preview-and-import every time. This PR adds a full automated sync pipeline: a background service polls all eligible claims hourly, a shared engine handles idempotent import logic, and the community admin UI surfaces sync health and per-claim controls.

## Backend

- **`ExternalSyncEngine`** (new scoped service) — extracts sync logic from `TriggerExternalSyncAsync` into a reusable engine used by both the manual mutation and the background service. Updates `LastSyncSucceededAtUtc` only on clean runs; records `LastSyncError` on failure.
- **`ExternalSourceSyncService`** (new `BackgroundService`) — runs every hour, queries for `Verified` + `IsAutoSyncEnabled = true` claims not synced within the last hour, calls `ExternalSyncEngine.SyncClaimAsync` per claim. Per-claim failures are isolated and logged without aborting the cycle.
- **`ExternalSourceClaim`** entity gains: `LastSyncSucceededAtUtc`, `LastSyncError`, `IsAutoSyncEnabled` (default `true`).
- **`SetAutoSyncEnabled` mutation** — lets group admins toggle auto-sync per claim without touching claim status.
- `TriggerExternalSyncAsync` now delegates to `ExternalSyncEngine` (no behavior change for manual sync callers).
- `AppDbInitializer` adds idempotent column migrations for the three new fields.

```csharp
// Background service core loop
var claims = await dbContext.ExternalSourceClaims
    .Where(c => c.Status == Verified && c.IsAutoSyncEnabled
             && (c.LastSyncAtUtc == null || c.LastSyncAtUtc < cutoff))
    .ToListAsync(cancellationToken);

foreach (var claim in claims)
    await engine.SyncClaimAsync(claim, claim.CreatedByUserId, cancellationToken);
```

## Frontend

- `ExternalSourceClaim` type gains `lastSyncSucceededAtUtc`, `lastSyncError`, `isAutoSyncEnabled`.
- `CommunityDetailView` source cards now show:
  - Last successful sync date (distinct from last attempt)
  - Inline error text when `lastSyncError` is set
  - Auto-sync on/off badge with tooltip
  - **Sync Now** button (direct trigger, no preview required)
  - **Enable / Disable auto-sync** toggle
- `communities` store exposes `setAutoSyncEnabled()`.
- All three locales (en/de/sk) updated with new keys.

## Tests

## Summary

- Add `buildProjectKnowledgeGuidance()` composable guidance function in the MessageBuilder system

## Design Decisions

This Phase 1 implements **content injection** (different from PR #1951's behavioral guidance for #1506):

| Dimension | PR #1951 (#1506) | This PR (#1916) |
|-----------|-------------------|-----------------|
| Approach | Behavioral guidance (tells agent to read CLAUDE.md) | Direct content injection |
| Loading | Agent uses Read tool at runtime | KnowledgeLoader reads files upfront |
| Scope | CLAUDE.md only | CLAUDE.md + knowledge directories |
| Integration | MessageBuilder guidance | MessageBuilder guidance + KnowledgeLoader |

The two approaches are **complementary**: behavioral guidance for project context discovery + content injection for persistent knowledge.

### Architecture

```
Config (knowledge section)
    ↓
KnowledgeLoader (file I/O)

projectKnowledgeContext string
    ↓

author: jlowhy
body:
## What was changed
This PR separates webhook payload authoring metadata from trigger parameter metadata by introducing provider-owned `payloadReferences` and switching the dashboard token catalog to consume that field end to end. GitHub webhook events now explicitly declare the `payload.*` tokens they support for authoring, and the control-plane and dashboard preserve that contract without inference.

Original symptom this addresses:
```text
The editor could omit valid payload.* completions or mark runtime-valid Liquid paths as invalid because it derived payload tokens from trigger parameters instead of the runtime payload authoring contract.
```

- `packages/integrations-core/src/types/index.ts`: adds the shared `IntegrationWebhookPayloadReference` contract with only `path` and required `description`.
- `packages/integrations-definitions/src/github/shared/supported-webhook-events.ts`: declares explicit GitHub `payloadReferences` for the webhook events currently used by the editor.
- `apps/control-plane-api/src/integration-targets/schemas.ts`: adds API schema support for `payloadReferences`.
- `apps/control-plane-api/src/integration-targets/services/resolve-target-metadata.ts`: clones `payloadReferences` through target metadata resolution without inference.
- `apps/dashboard/src/features/integrations/integrations-service-shared.ts`: accepts `payloadReferences` in the dashboard integration schema.
- `apps/dashboard/src/features/automations/webhook-automation-trigger-types.ts`: models `payloadReferences` on dashboard event options.
- `apps/dashboard/src/features/automations/webhook-automation-option-builders.ts`: preserves `payloadReferences` when mapping supported webhook events into UI event options.
- `apps/dashboard/src/features/automations/agent-instructions-token-catalog.ts`: removes parameter-derived payload token discovery and builds event-specific `payload.*` tokens only from `payloadReferences`.
- `apps/dashboard/src/features/automations/webhook-automation-test-fixtures.ts`: updates GitHub fixtures to declare payload references independently from trigger parameters.
- `apps/dashboard/src/features/automations/agent-instructions-token-catalog.test.ts`: rewrites regression coverage around the new boundary.
- `apps/dashboard/src/features/automations/webhook-automation-option-builders.test.ts`: covers preservation of payload references in built event options.
- `apps/control-plane-api/openapi/control-plane.v1.json`: regenerates the public OpenAPI spec for the new field.
- `apps/dashboard/src/lib/control-plane-api/generated/schema.ts`: regenerates the dashboard control-plane client schema.

## How to review
Start with the contract and ownership boundary, then follow the field through transport and into the dashboard consumer.

1. Read `packages/integrations-core/src/types/index.ts` to see the new shared shape.
2. Review `packages/integrations-definitions/src/github/shared/supported-webhook-events.ts` to confirm GitHub now declares payload authoring truth directly.
3. Review `apps/control-plane-api/src/integration-targets/schemas.ts` and `apps/control-plane-api/src/integration-targets/services/resolve-target-metadata.ts` to confirm the control plane only validates and copies the field.
4. Review `apps/dashboard/src/features/automations/webhook-automation-trigger-types.ts`, `apps/dashboard/src/features/integrations/integrations-service-shared.ts`, and `apps/dashboard/src/features/automations/webhook-automation-option-builders.ts` to confirm dashboard event options preserve the new field.
5. Finish with `apps/dashboard/src/features/automations/agent-instructions-token-catalog.ts` and its tests to verify the bug fix.

Local validation commands:
- `pnpm format`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test`

## What the implication was
The editor and runtime now share a single provider-owned payload authoring contract for webhook events. Trigger parameter metadata no longer leaks into token availability, so runtime-valid paths can be surfaced even when they are not part of trigger filtering UI.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Integration definitions\npayloadReferences] --> B[Control-plane metadata]
  B --> C[Dashboard event options]
  C --> D[Agent instructions token catalog]
  D --> E[Autocomplete and validation]
```

This also narrows responsibilities:
- integration definitions define which `payload.*` tokens exist and what they mean
- control plane transports the contract unchanged
- dashboard consumes the contract without fallback or locally curated payload metadata

## Checks and tests performed
- `pnpm format`
  - What is being tested: repository formatting for the touched TypeScript and generated schema files.
  - Expected outcome: formatting is current and no files need further normalization.
  - How it is implemented: runs `oxfmt` across the workspace.
- `pnpm lint`
  - What is being tested: static analysis, OpenAPI drift checks, docs lint, and Rust lint hooks.
  - Expected outcome: no lint violations and generated OpenAPI artifacts match committed outputs.
  - How it is implemented: runs workspace oxlint, control-plane/data-plane OpenAPI drift checks, docs lint, and Rust lint tasks.
- `pnpm typecheck`
  - What is being tested: the new `payloadReferences` contract across workspace packages and scripts.
  - Expected outcome: all packages and scripts typecheck successfully after the contract change.
  - How it is implemented: runs Turbo workspace typechecks plus the root scripts TypeScript project.
- `pnpm test`
  - What is being tested: workspace test suites after the event metadata and token-catalog changes.
  - Expected outcome: all affected and dependent tests continue to pass.
  - How it is implemented: runs the workspace test pipeline through Turbo.

author: michaelneale
body:
## Summary

Integrate Lemonade as an inference backend. Lemonade manages the full backend stack — GPU (llama.cpp), NPU (FLM, RyzenAI), whisper, stable-diffusion, TTS — so mesh-llm just proxies to it.

This is the simplest path to NPU inference: Lemonade already handles FLM subprocess lifecycle, NPU exclusivity, and multi-modal routing. No NPU-specific code needed in mesh-llm.

## Usage

```bash
# Lemonade-only mode (no --model needed)
mesh-llm --lemonade-port 8000

# Alongside a local model
mesh-llm --model Qwen3-8B --lemonade-port 8000
```

On AMD Ryzen AI hardware, Lemonade automatically uses FLM for NPU inference. mesh-llm proxies to it — models appear in `/v1/models` and are routable across the mesh.

## What Lemonade hosts

| Backend | Device | Capability |
|---------|--------|------------|
| llama.cpp | GPU (Metal, Vulkan, ROCm, CUDA) | LLM chat/completion |
| FastFlowLM | NPU (AMD Ryzen AI) | LLM, ASR, embeddings, reranking |
| RyzenAI | NPU (AMD Ryzen AI) | LLM (hybrid NPU) |
| whisper.cpp | CPU/NPU | Audio transcription |
| stable-diffusion.cpp | CPU/GPU | Image generation |
| Kokoro | CPU | Text-to-speech |

## Implementation

**Lemonade-only mode** (`--lemonade` with no `--model`):
- Connects to Lemonade, lists models, registers as local targets
- Starts API proxy — all requests forwarded to Lemonade
- No election loop, no rpc-server, no llama-server
- Death watchdog detects disconnect, cleans up

**Alongside local models** (`--model X --lemonade`):
- Lemonade models added as additional targets after election starts
- Primary model served via llama-server as usual

**Plugin inference registration** (future extension):
- Plugins can register any OpenAI-compatible backend via `notify_host("inference/register", {model, port, backend})`
- Generic: works for Lemonade, Ollama, vLLM, anything
- Plumbing is in place, not yet exercised by any plugin

## Changes

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `inference/lemonade.rs` | NEW — health check, model listing, external connect |
| `inference/launch.rs` | `InferenceServerHandle::external()` for unowned processes |
| `cli/mod.rs` | `--lemonade`, `--lemonade-port` flags |
| `runtime/mod.rs` | Lemonade-only startup path + integration with existing runtime |
| `plugin/mod.rs` | `PluginInferenceEvent` type + channel |
| `plugin/runtime.rs` | Thread inference_tx through plugin subprocess |
| `plugin/transport.rs` | Intercept `inference/register` notifications |

## Testing

```bash
cargo test -p mesh-llm                                          # 359 pass
cargo test -p mesh-llm lemonade_live -- --ignored --nocapture   # 4 pass (needs Lemonade running)
```

Live tested: proxy forwards chat completions to Lemonade 10.0.1, `/v1/models` returns Lemonade models.

## TODO

- [ ] Non-LLM endpoint proxying (whisper, SD, TTS, embeddings)
- [ ] Auto-discovery via UDP beacon
- [ ] Capabilities metadata in plugin inference registration

author: ukukdin
body:
## Summary
- Redis Sorted Set 기반 대기열 진입/순번 조회 API 구현 (`POST /queue/enter`, `GET /queue/position`)
- 스케줄러 기반 입장 토큰 발급 (100ms 주기, 18명씩 → Thundering Herd 완화)
- 토큰 TTL 5분, 주문 API 진입 시 `EntryTokenInterceptor`로 토큰 검증, 주문 완료 후 자동 소비
- 처리량 설계: DB 커넥션 풀 40 / 평균 200ms = 200 TPS → 안전 마진 70% = 175 TPS

## Changes
- **ErrorType**: 대기열 관련 에러 6종 추가 (QUEUE_FULL, QUEUE_NOT_FOUND, QUEUE_TOKEN_* 등)
- **WebMvcConfig**: `/api/v1/queue/**` 인증 경로 추가, `EntryTokenInterceptor` 등록
- **OrderService**: 주문 생성 후 `entryTokenRepository.delete(userId)` 토큰 소비
- **application.yml**: `queue.*` 설정 추가 (batch-size, token-ttl, throughput, scheduler interval)
- **batch-size-estimation.md**: 스케줄러 배치 크기 산정 근거 문서

## 리뷰 시 봐주시면 좋을 포인트

### 1. 대기열 도메인 설계 (`domain/model/queue/`)
- `QueuePosition`, `EntryToken`을 Value Object로 분리한 판단이 적절한지
- `QueueProperties`를 도메인 인터페이스(Port)로 두고 인프라에서 구현한 DIP 구조

### 2. Redis 읽기/쓰기 분리 (`infrastructure/queue/`)
- Master에 쓰기, Replica에 읽기를 분리했는데, 순번 조회 시 Replica 지연으로 인한 정합성 이슈가 있을 수 있는지
- `addIfAbsent`로 중복 방지 처리가 충분한지, 혹시 race condition이 있을 수 있는지

### 3. Thundering Herd 완화 전략
- 100ms 간격 × 18명 = 초당 ~180명 발급으로 설계했는데, 이 수치가 실제 DB 커넥션 풀(40) 대비 적정한지
- 토큰 발급 직후 동시 주문 호출이 몰리는 문제를 추가로 완화할 방법이 있을지 (Jitter 등)

### 4. 토큰 검증 인터셉터 위치
- `EntryTokenInterceptor`를 `AuthenticationInterceptor` 이후에 등록했는데, 인터셉터 체인 순서가 의도대로 동작하는지
- `POST /api/v1/orders`에만 적용되도록 메서드 체크를 인터셉터 내부에서 하는 방식 vs pathPattern으로 분리하는 방식

### 5. 스케줄러 단일 장애점
- `@Scheduled`로 단일 인스턴스에서만 동작하는데, 멀티 인스턴스 배포 시 중복 발급 방지 전략 (Redis 분산 락 등)
- 스케줄러가 죽었을 때 감지 및 복구 방안

### 6. Graceful Degradation
- 현재 Redis 장애 시 대기열 API가 전면 실패하는데, fallback 전략이 필요한지

## Test plan
- [x] QueueService 단위 테스트 17건 (진입/중복방지/순번조회/토큰검증/토큰발급/처리량초과)
- [x] QueueConcurrencyTest 통합 테스트 7건 (동시 진입, 토큰 TTL, 스케줄러 배치 크기, 혼합 동시성)
- [x] OrderServiceTest 기존 테스트 통과 확인
- ⚠️ 통합 테스트(`@SpringBootTest`)는 `RestrictedTransactionalEventListenerFactory` 컨텍스트 로드 이슈로 기존 동시성 테스트(Payment, Stock 등)와 동일하게 실패 — 별도 이슈로 해결 필요

## What

work on issue #762.

Closes #762

## Artifacts

| File | Path |
|------|------|
| Plan | `.flow-states/rust-foundation-hybrid-plan.md` |
| DAG | `.flow-states/rust-foundation-hybrid-dag.md` |
| Log | `.flow-states/rust-foundation-hybrid.log` |
| State | `.flow-states/rust-foundation-hybrid.json` |

## Plan

<details>
<summary>Implementation plan</summary>

```text
# Plan: Hybrid Dispatcher + CI Integration

## Context

Issue #762: Implement the hybrid dispatcher for the Rust migration's strangler fig
pattern. The Rust project structure already exists (PRs #796, #797) with state types,
shared utilities, file locking, output helpers, git/github wrappers, and phase config.
The dispatcher is the bridge that lets commands be ported from Python to Rust one at a
time without disrupting the existing workflow.

## Exploration

**Current dispatcher (`bin/flow`, 26 lines):** Pure bash — resolves `$LIB_DIR` relative
to its own directory, checks `$subcmd.py` exists in lib/, then `exec python3 "$script"`.

**Rust binary (`src/main.rs`):** Clap CLI with an empty `Commands` enum. No subcommands
implemented. Builds successfully to `target/debug/flow-rs`.

**CI (`bin/ci`):** Runs pymarkdown, ruff check, ruff format, pytest. No Rust steps.
GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) only sets up Python 3.14.

**Test runner (`bin/test`):** Runs `pytest --no-cov "$@"`. No Rust support.

**Existing tests:**
- `tests/test_bin_flow.py` — runs real `bin/flow` via subprocess, tests dispatch, args, exit codes
- `tests/test_bin_ci.py` — `ci_project` fixture creates minimal project with bin/ci, lib/, tests/, .venv/
- `tests/test_bin_test.py` — `test_project` fixture creates minimal project with bin/test, tests/, .venv/
- `tests/roundtrip.rs` — Rust integration test for state serialization

**Settings:** `.claude/settings.json` already allows `Bash(cargo build *)`, `Bash(cargo test *)`,
`Bash(cargo check *)`, `Bash(cargo clippy *)`, `Bash(cargo fmt *)`.

## Risks

1. **`set -e` vs exit 127:** `bin/flow` uses `set -euo pipefail`. Running the Rust binary
   with exit 127 would terminate the script immediately. Must temporarily disable errexit
   for the Rust binary call and capture the exit code.

2. **Binary path resolution in target projects:** `bin/flow` runs in target projects via
   `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/flow`. The Rust binary lives relative to the script
   (`$SCRIPT_DIR/../target/`). This works for both the FLOW repo (local bin/flow) and
   target projects (plugin cache bin/flow) — the binary would be in the plugin's target/.

3. **CI needs Rust toolchain:** GitHub Actions workflow needs `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`
   added. Without it, `cargo test` fails in CI.

4. **Rust binary output on exit 127:** The binary must produce no stdout on exit 127. Any
   output would mix with the Python fallback's output. Only stderr is safe (and optional).

## Approach

- Use clap's `external_subcommand` feature to catch unrecognized commands and exit 127
  silently (no stdout). As commands get ported, add new enum variants above the catch-all.
- The dispatcher checks for the binary at `target/release/flow-rs` then `target/debug/flow-rs`
  (relative to its own directory). Tries it, captures exit code. If 127, falls through to
  Python. Any other exit code passes through directly.
- `bin/ci` adds `cargo test` conditionally when `Cargo.toml` exists in `$REPO_ROOT`.
- `bin/test` adds `--rust` flag to run `cargo test` instead of pytest.

## Dependency Graph

| Task | Type | Depends On |
|------|------|------------|
| 1. Write Rust exit-127 integration tests | test | — |
| 2. Implement exit-127 in main.rs | implement | 1 |
| 3. Write hybrid dispatcher Python tests | test | 2 |
| 4. Implement hybrid dispatcher in bin/flow | implement | 3 |
| 5. Write bin/ci cargo integration tests | test | — |
| 6. Implement cargo test in bin/ci | implement | 5 |
| 7. Write bin/test --rust tests | test | — |
| 8. Implement --rust flag in bin/test | implement | 7 |
| 9. Update CI workflow for Rust toolchain | implement | 6 |

## Tasks

### Task 1: Write Rust exit-127 integration tests

Add `tests/dispatcher.rs` with integration tests:
- `unknown_subcommand_exits_127` — run `flow-rs nonexistent-command`, assert exit code 127
- `unknown_subcommand_no_stdout` — verify no stdout output on exit 127 (clean for fallback)
- `no_subcommand_exits_1` — run `flow-rs` with no args, assert exit code 1
- `help_flag_exits_0` — run `flow-rs --help`, assert exit 0

Use `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_flow-rs")` for binary path. Pattern matches existing
`tests/roundtrip.rs` integration test structure.

Files: `tests/dispatcher.rs`

### Task 2: Implement exit-127 in main.rs

Modify `src/main.rs`:
- Add `#[command(external_subcommand)] External(Vec<String>)` variant to `Commands` enum
- `External(_)` match arm calls `std::process::exit(127)` — no stdout output
- `None` (no subcommand) prints message to stderr and exits 1
- Keep `--help` and `--version` handled by clap normally

Files: `src/main.rs`

### Task 3: Write hybrid dispatcher Python tests

Add tests to `tests/test_bin_flow.py`:
- `test_hybrid_falls_back_when_rust_exits_127` — create a temp project with bin/flow
  (copied from real), a mock Rust binary (exits 127), and a Python script. Verify Python
  handles the command.
- `test_hybrid_passes_through_rust_exit_code` — mock Rust binary exits 0 with output.
  Verify output comes from Rust and exit code is 0. Also test non-zero non-127 exit.
- `test_dispatcher_works_without_rust_binary` — no target/ directory. Verify Python
  handles the command (existing behavior preserved).

Use a `hybrid_project` fixture that creates: bin/flow (copied), lib/<cmd>.py, and
optionally target/debug/flow-rs (mock bash script). Pattern matches the self-contained
fixture approach in test_bin_ci.py.

Files: `tests/test_bin_flow.py`

### Task 4: Implement hybrid dispatcher in bin/flow

Modify `bin/flow` to add Rust-first routing after resolving `$subcmd`:
- Resolve `RUST_BIN` at `$SCRIPT_DIR/../target/release/flow-rs` then `$SCRIPT_DIR/../target/debug/flow-rs`
- If `$RUST_BIN` is executable, run `"$RUST_BIN" "$subcmd" "$@"` with errexit disabled
- If exit code is not 127, exit with that code (success or failure from Rust)
- If exit code is 127, fall through to Python path (existing logic)
- If no Rust binary exists, fall through to Python path (existing behavior)

Files: `bin/flow`

### Task 5: Write bin/ci cargo integration tests

Add tests to `tests/test_bin_ci.py`:
- `test_runs_cargo_test_when_cargo_toml_exists` — add a Cargo.toml and minimal Rust project
  to ci_project fixture, use a mock cargo binary that echoes a marker. Verify marker appears
  in output.
- `test_skips_cargo_when_no_cargo_toml` — standard ci_project (no Cargo.toml). Verify no
  cargo invocation (use mock cargo that would error if called).

The mock cargo approach avoids needing a real Rust toolchain in the test fixture. Create a
mock `cargo` script in a temp bin dir and prepend it to PATH.

Files: `tests/test_bin_ci.py`

### Task 6: Implement cargo test in bin/ci

Modify `bin/ci` to add cargo test after the Python test steps:
- Check `if [ -f "$REPO_ROOT/Cargo.toml" ]`
- If true, run `cargo test`
- Place after pytest so Python tests still run even if Cargo.toml exists but Rust fails

Files: `bin/ci`

### Task 7: Write bin/test --rust tests

Add tests to `tests/test_bin_test.py`:
- `test_rust_flag_runs_cargo_test` — pass `--rust` to bin/test, verify cargo test is invoked
  (mock cargo approach)
- `test_rust_flag_passes_extra_args` — `--rust test_name` passes remaining args to cargo test
- `test_default_still_runs_pytest` — no `--rust` flag, existing pytest behavior unchanged

Files: `tests/test_bin_test.py`

### Task 8: Implement --rust flag in bin/test

Modify `bin/test`:
- If first argument is `--rust`, shift and run `cargo test "$@"`
- Otherwise, existing pytest behavior (unchanged)

Files: `bin/test`

author: dirtysololil
body:
### Motivation
- SSR auth checks in the web app could not reliably derive the API base URL in the Next standalone runtime, causing `fetchViewer()`/`requireViewer()` to return null and `/app` to immediately redirect back to `/login` despite a valid session. 
- The PM2 `lobby-web` process did not forward `WEB_PUBLIC_URL`/`API_PUBLIC_URL` (and `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`) into the standalone Next process, which worsened SSR URL resolution in production. 
- Silent failures and missing diagnostics in the login/session flow made the problem hard to observe and recover from. 
- The client post-login navigation was brittle and could race with cookie persistence checks, producing the observed refresh loop. 

### Description
- Added a server-request fallback `resolveApiBaseUrlForServerRequest()` to `apps/web/src/lib/runtime-config.ts` that derives the API URL from `x-forwarded-host` / `x-forwarded-proto` so SSR code can resolve API URL when `API_PUBLIC_URL` is not injected. 
- Switched server-side helpers to use the fallback and always forward request cookies, and added safe diagnostic logs for missing API URL, unauthorized responses and request failures in `apps/web/src/lib/server-session.ts` and `apps/web/src/lib/server-api.ts`. 
- Made client login flow more robust by verifying `GET /v1/auth/me` after `POST /v1/auth/login` and using `router.replace('/app')` + `router.refresh()` for a stable post-login transition, in `apps/web/src/components/auth/login-form.tsx`. 
- Hardened API CORS origin checking and enabled credentials with normalized origin matching in `apps/api/src/main.ts`, and added concise auth cookie set/clear logs in `apps/api/src/modules/auth/auth-cookie.util.ts`. 
- Added lightweight auth diagnostics logs in `apps/api/src/modules/auth/auth.controller.ts` and `apps/api/src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts` to trace login success/failure and session creation. 
- Updated `ecosystem.config.cjs` to forward `WEB_PUBLIC_URL`/`API_PUBLIC_URL` and corresponding `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` env vars into the standalone `lobby-web` process. 

### Testing
- Prettier formatting was run and fixed style issues across modified files and completed successfully. 
- `pnpm --filter @lobby/api build` succeeded (Nest build passed). 
- `pnpm --filter @lobby/web build` was executed with explicit env (APP_NAME, WEB_PUBLIC_URL, API_PUBLIC_URL, MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL, REALTIME_PUBLIC_URL, REALTIME_PATH, WEB_PORT, WEB_HOST, MAX_AVATAR_*) and Next build completed successfully, then failed in this environment during packaging due to a pre-existing missing `apps/web/public` directory (unrelated to auth fixes). 
- Full `pnpm build` in the current environment fails when required web env vars are not set, which is expected until production env variables are injected into the standalone process.

## Summary
Centralize magic numbers into constants config

## Description
## Problem/Goal

Timeout values, intervals, and limits are scattered as inline magic numbers across multiple files. This makes it hard to tune configuration and understand the system's timing behavior at a glance.

## Approach

1. **Create `packages/backend/src/config/constants.ts`** with all backend-specific timing constants:
   ```typescript
   export const TIMEOUTS = {
     // WebSocket
     WS_TICKET_TTL_MS: 30_000,              // routes/auth.ts:20 (already a const, move here)
     WS_TICKET_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS: 60_000, // routes/auth.ts:52 (currently inline)
     DEVICE_PING_INTERVAL_MS: 30_000,       // websocket/handlers/device.ts:12 (already a const, move here)
     
     // Authentication
     OTP_EXPIRATION_MS: 15 * 60 * 1000,     // routes/auth.ts:87 (currently inline: 15 * 60 * 1000)
     OTP_REQUEST_COOLDOWN_S: 60,            // routes/auth.ts:79 (currently inline: 60)
     
     // Device pairing
     PAIRING_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_MS: 5 * 60 * 1000, // routes/devices.ts:134 (currently inline: 5 * 60 * 1000)
   }
   ```
   Note: Call-related timeouts (`RING_TIMEOUT_MS`, `ICE_GATHERING_TIMEOUT_MS`, `CALL_SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS`) are already properly defined in `packages/shared/src/webrtc/constants.ts` — do NOT duplicate them.

2. **Update files to import from constants**:
   - `routes/auth.ts:20` — replace `WS_TICKET_TTL_MS = 30_000` with import
   - `routes/auth.ts:52` — replace inline `60_000` with `TIMEOUTS.WS_TICKET_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS`
   - `routes/auth.ts:79` — replace inline `60` with `TIMEOUTS.OTP_REQUEST_COOLDOWN_S`
   - `routes/auth.ts:87` — replace `15 * 60 * 1000` with `TIMEOUTS.OTP_EXPIRATION_MS`
   - `routes/devices.ts:134` — replace `5 * 60 * 1000` with `TIMEOUTS.PAIRING_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_MS`
   - `websocket/handlers/device.ts:12` — replace `PING_INTERVAL = 30000` with import

## Key Files

- `packages/backend/src/config/constants.ts` — new file
- `packages/backend/src/routes/auth.ts` — lines 20, 52, 79, 87
- `packages/backend/src/routes/devices.ts` — line 134
- `packages/backend/src/websocket/handlers/device.ts` — line 12

## Important Notes

- Do NOT touch constants already in `packages/shared/src/webrtc/constants.ts` — those are shared between frontend and backend and are already well-organized
- Keep the constants file focused on backend-only values
- Use descriptive names with units in the suffix (`_MS` for milliseconds, `_S` for seconds)
- This is a pure refactor — no behavior changes, no value changes

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `config/constants.ts` created with all identified magic numbers
- [ ] All inline magic numbers replaced with constant imports
- [ ] No duplicate constants between backend and shared packages
- [ ] All existing tests pass
- [ ] No value changes — this is a move, not a tune

body:
Flat `ESP32CanBus/` directory mixed standalone sketches, production firmware, and web assets with no clear hierarchy. No root README, no .gitignore, and `.pio/` build artifacts were committed to the repo.

## Structure
Reorganized `ESP32CanBus/` → `firmware/` with named sub-folders:
- `esp32s3-can-logger/` — main production firmware (ESP32-S3)
- `esp32-gps-logger/` — GPS + CAN logger for original ESP32 Dev Module
- `can-commander/` — reusable serial CAN commander module
- `tools/` — utility/test sketches (hardware test, flash erase, SPIFFS reformat)

## Documentation
- **`README.md`** (root, new) — badges, feature matrix, hardware BOM, pin tables, Arduino IDE + PlatformIO quick-start, full Web UI / REST / WebSocket API reference, OBD-II PID table, ESP-NOW and SD logging sections
- **`docs/hardware.md`** — wiring diagrams for both ESP32-S3 and ESP32 Dev Module variants, OBD-II J1962 connector pinout, power budget, CAN termination notes
- **`docs/obd2-pids.md`** — Service 01 PID formula reference (16 PIDs: RPM, speed, temps, fuel, O₂, odometer, etc.) with request/response frame format
- Sub-folder `README.md` added for each `firmware/` directory; `esp32s3-can-logger/README.md` updated with cross-links to root docs

## Housekeeping
